cv-70883c8c.stem: A young woman develops severe vomiting and bloating after meals following rapid weight loss; the duodenum is found to be compressed between the aorta and a vessel. Which vessel is it, and which part of the duodenum is affected?
options: Superior mesenteric artery – third (horizontal) part of the duodenum
Inferior mesenteric artery – fourth part of the duodenum
Coeliac trunk – first part of the duodenum
Left renal artery – second part of the duodenum
Hepatic portal vein – first part of the duodenum
cv-70883c8c.explanation: The horizontal part of the duodenum passes between the aorta and the SMA at L3. When retroperitoneal fat is lost, the angle between them narrows and the duodenum is compressed (SMA syndrome, Wilkie syndrome).

cv-0614100a.stem: Which area of the colonic blood supply, known as a 'watershed', is most vulnerable to ischaemia?
options: Lower rectum
Middle of the ascending colon
Caecum
Right colic flexure
Left colic flexure (meeting of the SMA and IMA territories)
cv-0614100a.explanation: The left colic flexure (Griffiths' point) is where the end territories of the SMA's middle colic artery and the IMA's left colic artery meet and where the marginal artery (of Drummond) may be weak. The rectosigmoid junction (Sudeck's point) is the other critical area.

cv-bc394f94.stem: Which artery, the terminal branch of the inferior mesenteric artery, supplies the upper rectum?
options: Sigmoid artery
Superior rectal artery
Inferior rectal artery
Median sacral artery
Middle rectal artery
cv-bc394f94.explanation: The IMA (L3) gives the left colic artery, the sigmoid arteries and the superior rectal artery. The middle rectal artery arises from the internal iliac artery and the inferior rectal artery from the internal pudendal artery.

cv-34e1fdec.stem: Which statement about the renal arteries is correct?
options: The right renal artery passes behind the inferior vena cava.
There are wide anastomoses between the segmental arteries.
They arise from the aorta at T10.
They run in front of the renal veins.
The left renal artery is longer than the right.
cv-34e1fdec.explanation: The renal arteries arise at L1–L2; because the aorta lies to the left, the right renal artery is longer and passes behind the IVC. At the hilum the order from front to back is vein, artery, pelvis. The segmental arteries are end arteries.

cv-23038544.stem: Which artery arises from the posterior trunk of the internal iliac artery?
options: Superior gluteal artery
Uterine artery
Inferior gluteal artery
Obturator artery
Internal pudendal artery
cv-23038544.explanation: The posterior trunk gives the iliolumbar artery, the lateral sacral arteries and the superior gluteal artery. The anterior trunk gives the visceral branches (umbilical, inferior vesical/vaginal, uterine and middle rectal arteries) and the parietal branches (obturator, internal pudendal and inferior gluteal arteries).

cv-20f3067b.stem: The inferior epigastric artery is a branch of which artery?
options: Internal iliac artery
Obturator artery
External iliac artery
Femoral artery
Internal thoracic artery
cv-20f3067b.explanation: The inferior epigastric artery arises from the external iliac artery just above the inguinal ligament, rises medial to the deep inguinal ring and anastomoses in the rectus sheath with the superior epigastric artery (a branch of the internal thoracic artery).

cv-f36779f3.stem: Which statement about the bifurcation of the common iliac artery is correct?
options: It lies in front of the sacroiliac joint, and the ureter usually crosses the iliac vessels here.
It lies at L1, at the hilum of the kidneys.
Beyond this point the internal iliac artery descends into the thigh.
The ductus deferens passes behind the bifurcation.
The inferior vena cava passes in front of this point.
cv-f36779f3.explanation: The common iliac arteries divide into the internal and external iliac arteries in front of the sacroiliac joint. At the pelvic inlet the ureter passes in front of this bifurcation; this is one of the physiological narrowings of the ureter, where stones lodge.

cv-6134b2af.stem: Where is the femoral pulse best felt?
options: At the level of the adductor hiatus
Just above the pubic tubercle
Behind the greater trochanter
In the middle of the thigh, at the lateral border of sartorius
Below the inguinal ligament, midway between the ASIS and the pubic symphysis (mid-inguinal point)
cv-6134b2af.explanation: The femoral artery enters the femoral triangle under the inguinal ligament and is felt at the mid-inguinal point by pressing it against bone (femoral head, pubis). It is the artery most used for catheterisation; the vein lies just medial to it.

cv-dba30b16.stem: What are the branches of the profunda femoris artery?
options: External pudendal and inferior epigastric arteries
Medial circumflex femoral, lateral circumflex femoral and perforating arteries
Descending genicular and popliteal arteries
Superficial epigastric and superficial circumflex iliac arteries
Obturator and inferior gluteal arteries
cv-dba30b16.explanation: The deep femoral artery is the main supply of the thigh; the two circumflex arteries supply the region of the hip and the perforating arteries the posterior compartment of the thigh. The medial circumflex artery is the main source of blood for the femoral head.

cv-d4ddc968.stem: What is the order of structures in the popliteal fossa from superficial to deep?
options: Popliteal vein – tibial nerve – popliteal artery
Popliteal artery – tibial nerve – popliteal vein
Popliteal artery – popliteal vein – tibial nerve
Tibial nerve – popliteal vein – popliteal artery
Tibial nerve – popliteal artery – popliteal vein
cv-d4ddc968.explanation: In the popliteal fossa the nerve is most superficial, the vein in the middle and the artery deepest (against the femur and the knee capsule). So the popliteal pulse is felt by pressing deeply with the knee slightly bent, and the artery can be injured in supracondylar fractures of the femur.

cv-eefdaca9.stem: Where is the dorsalis pedis pulse best felt?
options: At the base of the 5th metatarsal
Behind the medial malleolus
On the inner side of the heel
In front of the lateral malleolus
On the dorsum of the foot, lateral to the extensor hallucis longus tendon
cv-eefdaca9.explanation: The dorsalis pedis artery continues the anterior tibial artery; on the dorsum of the foot it is felt just lateral to the EHL tendon, between the 1st and 2nd metatarsals. It is one of the first pulses lost in peripheral arterial disease.

cv-c38d2770.stem: The fibular (peroneal) artery is a branch of which artery?
options: Posterior tibial artery
A direct branch of the popliteal artery
Dorsalis pedis artery
Femoral artery
Anterior tibial artery
cv-c38d2770.explanation: The posterior tibial artery gives off the fibular artery in the upper leg; it runs close to the fibula and supplies the lateral compartment muscles through perforating branches. The free fibula flap is raised on this artery.

cv-86d9b694.stem: Which arteries take part in the cruciate anastomosis of the hip region?
options: Iliolumbar and lateral sacral arteries
Superior gluteal, obturator and internal pudendal arteries
Inferior gluteal artery, medial and lateral circumflex femoral arteries and the 1st perforating artery
Inferior epigastric and obturator arteries
Genicular branches of the popliteal artery
cv-86d9b694.explanation: The cruciate anastomosis lies behind the femur at the level of the lesser trochanter and provides a collateral path between the internal iliac and femoral systems. It is important in proximal occlusion of the femoral artery.

cv-d936dd1e.stem: In a patient in shock in whom no peripheral vein can be found, which vein is the most reliable site for an emergency venous cut-down?
options: External jugular vein – in the neck
Great saphenous vein – in front of the medial malleolus
Small saphenous vein – behind the lateral malleolus
Cephalic vein – in the deltopectoral groove
Basilic vein – on the inner side of the elbow
cv-d936dd1e.explanation: The great saphenous vein is constant and superficial just in front of the medial malleolus, which makes it the classic cut-down site. Here the saphenous nerve runs with the vein and must be protected during the procedure.

cv-0c9c8933.stem: Into which vein does the great saphenous vein drain?
options: Internal iliac vein
Femoral vein (at the saphenous opening)
Profunda femoris vein
External iliac vein
Popliteal vein
cv-0c9c8933.explanation: The great saphenous vein rises on the inner thigh and passes through the fascia lata at the saphenous opening, about 3–4 cm below and lateral to the pubic tubercle, to drain into the femoral vein. It is used as a graft in coronary bypass.
